## The connectivity picture

Eight files carry `high_fan_in_fan_out`. They split into two very different kinds of hotspot, and the distinction drives the whole triage:

| File | fan-in | fan-out | Also has | test_gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | **18** (p99 = 10) | 1 | large_file 425L, 7× sync I/O | 0 |
| `src/plugin.ts` | 10 (= p99) | 3 | `buildFinished` 103L | 0.5 |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 (= p95) | 0 | 2 unprefixed booleans | 0.5 |
| `test/utils.ts` | 9 (= p95) | 0 | 1× sync I/O | 0 |
| `src/index.ts` | 4 | **17** (p99 = 11) | large_file 460L, 6 God functions | 0 |
| `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 | 11 (= p99) | `runEsbuild` 237L, 38-field option bag | 0.5 |
| `src/rollup.ts` | 0 | 7 | `getRollupConfig` 122L | 0.5 |
| `src/api-extractor.ts` | 1 | 6 (= p95) | `rollupDtsFiles` 85L | 0.5 |

**High fan-in is where blast radius lives; high fan-out is where comprehension cost lives.** Splitting a fan-in hub shrinks what 18 other files depend on. Splitting a fan-out orchestrator helps nobody but itself — `src/rollup.ts` has fan-in 0, so no amount of refactoring it reduces anyone else's risk.

Also worth deduplicating before you count work: `crime_00008/00009/00010` are one nested region (`build` 167–459 contains the anonymous 183–456 contains `mainTasks` 260–453), and `postcss.ts` 00002/00004 are the same plugin/setup pair. Six "God Function" findings in `src/index.ts` are really two refactors.

## Triage order

**1. `src/utils.ts` — do this first.**
Fan-in 18 against a p99 cutoff of 10; nothing else in the repo is close. 425 lines (1.4× threshold) and `blast_radius_importers: 29`. It is the only file that is simultaneously the top blast-radius hub *and* has a real structural defect — 18 importers each take a dependency on a 425-line module to use a slice of it. Split by responsibility (fs helpers / path helpers / the `removeFiles`+`ensureTempDeclarationDir` I/O group flagged by `crime_00060`), keep `utils.ts` as a re-export barrel so no importer changes on landing. `fan-out: 1` means the split can't cascade into other modules, and `test_gap: 0` means you have coverage to land it against. Highest leverage, lowest risk of any pick here.

**2. `src/index.ts` — second, and it's function extraction, not a file split.**
Highest fan-out in the repo (17 vs p99 of 11) and 460 lines, but fan-in is only **4** — this is an orchestrator, so restructuring is contained. The 293-line `build` with its 274-line nested arrow and 194-line `mainTasks` is where the fan-out actually comes from: extract `buildAll` (75L), `startWatcher` (79L), and `normalizeOptions` (96L) into modules and the 17 imports move with them, cutting both fan-out and file size in one pass. Fix `crime_00033` (`build` is named as a pure transform but calls `createLogger`/`removeFiles`) while you're inside it — misleading names on a 17-import orchestrator are exactly the agent-risk case.

**3. `src/plugin.ts` — third, and deliberately narrow.**
Fan-in 10 sits right at the p99 cutoff with 29 transitive importers — this is load-bearing, and `test_gap: 0.5` means the safety net is thinner than for utils/index. Do *not* take the finding's `split or invert` advice here; the file has no large_file finding, so its coupling is about what it exports, not its size. Extract `buildFinished` (103L, `crime_00007`) internally and stop. Additive changes only, exactly as `treat_as_load_bearing` suggests.

**4. `src/esbuild/index.ts` — fourth.**
Fan-out 11 (at p99), `runEsbuild` at 237 lines — 4× threshold — with a 38-property option bag (`crime_00054`) and 2× `Date.now()` (`crime_00012`). Genuinely the worst single function in the repo by comprehension cost. It ranks fourth only because fan-in is **1**: cleaning it up buys a lot of agent-editability and almost no blast-radius reduction. `test_gap: 0.5` also means you'd want characterization tests first, which is why it isn't cheap.

## Leave alone

- **`src/log.ts`** (fan-in 9, fan-out 0, 30 transitive importers). Widest footprint in the repo and *no* size or complexity finding — its only crimes are two unprefixed booleans. A leaf that 9 files depend on and that has nothing structurally wrong with it is working as intended. Touching it means touching 9 importers for zero gain. Rename `onlyImportant`/`silent` locally if you're already in the file; otherwise skip.
- **`src/rollup.ts`** (fan-in **0**, fan-out 7). `getRollupConfig` is 122 lines with a name/behaviour mismatch, but `blast_radius: 0` / `blast_radius_importers: 0` — nothing imports it. Whatever you fix here reduces risk for exactly one file. Opportunistic only.
- **`src/api-extractor.ts`** (fan-out 6, fan-in 1). Sits *exactly* on the p95 cutoff — it's the boundary case that makes the tier, not a hotspot. `rollupDtsFiles` at 85 lines is 1.4× threshold. Noise at this stage.
- **`test/utils.ts`** (fan-in 9). Real hub, but its 9 importers are all tests; blast radius is bounded to the suite and can't reach production behaviour.
- **`docs/README.md`** (679 lines, `high`, the top-severity large_file). It's markdown: `blast_radius: 0`, no importers, nothing parses it. It ranks high on severity because the detector is language-agnostic, not because it's load-bearing. Do not spend refactoring budget here — this is the clearest example in the report of severity ≠ blast radius.

## One caveat on the ordering

Picks 3 and 4 (`plugin.ts`, `esbuild/index.ts`) both carry `test_gap: 0.5`, and the report has 16 `weak_test_signal` findings — 11 tests with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls. The plan above front-loads the two files with `test_gap: 0` deliberately so the first two refactors land against real coverage. If you reorder to hit `runEsbuild` first, add characterization tests before you start, because the existing `test/` suite will pass whether or not you break it.
